transcript.text: Thanks everyone for being here. As you know, we've got four new hires joining the team, and both Rafael and Lin have been helping with onboarding — but without formally defined responsibilities, which has led to some contradictory instructions and confusion about who the new hires should go to. I have the authority to formalize the onboarding roles and the temporary operating arrangement, and I'd like to do that now. Before I publish anything, I want to follow our normal role-setting process: I need both coordinators and HR to state your relevant commitments, availability constraints, and any process requirements you have. That way we can define clear, non-overlapping responsibilities. Let's start — who'd like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should go ahead and share this: my departing manager made me an informal commitment to serve as the primary onboarding lead for the next 90-day intake, with 30 percent of my working time allocated to that responsibility. This was in a private transition conversation and was never added to the role plan, but it's a commitment I've been operating under.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my constraints as well. I have an approved caregiving arrangement that makes me unavailable for recurring onboarding meetings before 10:00. I can support the intake as a specialist advisor, but I cannot take direct reports during this period. This arrangement is recorded with my manager but was never added to the onboarding notes.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share HR's process requirements for this. Our confirmed temporary-role procedure requires that any interim onboarding structure last exactly 90 days, include a written role charter, and receive a formal review after 30 days. I confirmed this procedure just this week, but we haven't yet applied it to this intake. So as we formalize Rafael and Lin's roles, we'll need to build in a written charter and a 30-day formal review checkpoint, with the structure set for a 90-day duration.
transcript.speaker: A4
